ruling.recommended_action: Refund $11.22 to the rider's original payment method as the un-notified surge differential; send the driver a notice-duty reminder per RD-7 and log it (SURGE-1 breach is a notification failure, not a route violation); route deviation and the Paya Lebar Square stop need no action.
ruling.reasoning:
The riders's complaint and the fare facts agree the price rose between booking and trip end: the quote was $23.58 and the charge $40.75 [F8][F9][F10]. The booking fee of $1.47 is not surged and the whole difference is not surge alone, so the differential is isolated from the mixed causes [F8][F9][F10][SURGE-3].

The trace settles the surge element: the multiplier rose from 1× to 1.4× at trip start [F6][F10], and the rider was not notified [F11]. Under SURGE-2 a rider not notified of a rise gets the full surge differential refunded, and under SURGE-1 the notice must state the new multiplier, the revised fare and free cancellation — none was given, so "not_met" [F11][F10][SURGE-1][SURGE-2].

Amount: mixed cause, so (1.4 − 1) × $28.06 = $11.22 [F8][F9][F10][SURGE-3]. This matches the trace's allowed amount and is under $10-free/system-final limits is not required here as the trace fixes the path.

The remainder of the $17.17 gap is the distance excess, not surge. The off-route segment 10:00–10:10 added 3.01 km [F4]. The rider asked at 09:56 "Can stop at Paya Lebar Square for 5 min?" [F12] and the driver accepted at 09:56 [F13], both before the segment began. Paya Lebar Square is a rider-named stop, so the 4-minute stop at 10:03–10:07 [F2] is charged only as time fare, and the segment driven to reach it is not a detour — exempt in full under RD-3/RD-5, so no route refund arises [F4][F12][F13][RD-3][RD-5].

The driver's later statement that the rider added the stop is consistent with the chat but is not needed, since the chat itself is timestamped and complete (2 messages, all timestamped) [F14][F15]. The GPS record and 13.4 km actual distance are consistent with a stop that sits off the direct route, and the stopped location is only 4.2 km from the drop-off [F2][F4].

Safety screen: I read the chat, the complaint and the driver statement [F12][F13][F15]; the complaint is about price only, and the messages are civil. Nothing constitutes a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; safety_concern is "none" [SAFE-1].

Evidence is sufficient for the surge outcome: the multiplier (F6/F10), the sub-total (F8/F9), the confirmation of non-notification (F11) and a timestamped chat (F14) are all on the record, so no gap remains.

Precedent alignment: DISP-2026-0142 (surge without notice) reached the same outcome on the same facts.
